narr: Thunderstorms formed along a stationary boundary located draped across west-central and northwest GA on the 28th and 29th. Significant tropical moisture ahead of Hurricane Idalia led to several thunderstorms becoming strong to severe. The main hazards included damaging winds and torrential rainfall.
ev: The public reported flash flooding in the westbound lane of I-20 near mile marker 37, due to highwater on Slater Mill Creek. Radar estimates indicate that between 3 and 4 inches of rain occurred over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported flooding at the intersection of Bright Star Road and Central Church Road. Radar estimates indicate that between 5 and 6 inches of rain occurred over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported flooding near the intersection of Jodeco Road and Cook Lane. Radar estimates indicate that between 3 and 4 inches of rain occurred over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported flooding of the road near the intersection of Watkins Road and Ada Street. Radar estimates indicate that between 4 and 4.5 inches of rain occurred over the area, resulting in the flash flooding of Dry Creek and it's tributaries, inundating the roadway.

The Emergency Manager reported significant flooding near Meeks Parks from high water on Butternut Creek where the creek flows into Nottely River. Floodwaters caused several sinkholes and washed out culverts. Radar estimates indicate that between 5 and 6 inches of rain occurred over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported flooding near the Mall of Georgia, including at the intersection of Buford Drive and Rock Springs Road, and flooding at an apartment complex in the 2700 block of Mall of Georgia Boulevard. Radar estimates indicate that between 6 and 7 inches of rain occurred over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.
The Emergency Manager reported flooding at Dorsett Shoals Road and Kings Highway. Radar estimates indicate that between 3 and 4 inches of rain occurred over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported the closure of the Buford Highway and Fox Street intersection due to runoff into Sweetwater Creek flooding the roadway. Radar estimates indicate that between 6 and 7 inches of rain occurred over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported flooding at an apartment complex along College Street. Radar estimates indicate that between 6 and 8 inches of rain occurred over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager relayed a report of a water rescue from a stalled vehicle in the flood waters in Atlanta. Radar estimates indicate that between 1.5 and 2 inches of rain occurred over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported the intersection of Roswell Road and Sandy Springs Circle is closed in both directions due to flooding of the roadway. Additionally I-285 westbound at GA 400 was impassable with stalled vehicles. Radar estimates indicate that between 3.5 and 5 inches of rain occurred over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.
The Emergency Manager reported flooding in the roadway with multiple stranded vehicles.

The Emergency Manager relayed a report of flooding of the roadway at several points along Highway 83 near and southeast of Good Hope. Radar estimates indicate that between 6 and 7 inches of rain occurred over the northern portion of Morgan county, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported flooding over the roadway near the 6300 block of Sandy Creek Road. Radar estimates indicate that between 5 and 6 inches of rain occurred over the area, resulting in the flash flooding of the nearby creek and roadway.

The Emergency Manager reported water over Humphrey Mill Road near Hothouse Creek. Radar estimates indicate that between 4 and 4.5 inches of rain occurred over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported flooding along the 3900 block of Abbotts Bridge Road, and at the intersection of Duluth Highway and Buford Highway where floodwaters stalled vehicles. Radar estimates indicate that between 6 and 7 inches of rain occurred over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported flooding along and between Douglas Boulevard and Parkway Drive, due to highwater on a tributary of Anneewakee Creek. Radar estimates indicate that between 3 and 4 inches of rain occurred over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported I-285 westbound in Dunwoody was impassable due to water on the road. Radar estimates indicate that between 2 and 2.5 inches of rain occurred over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported flooding near the intersection of Fairplay Road and Mt Vernon Road due to high water on Big Sandy Creek. Radar estimates indicate that between 6 and 7 inches of rain occurred over the northern portion of Morgan county, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported flooding along Beechnut Lane and around homes. The flooding was due to highwater on Rose Creek and nearby ponds. Radar estimates indicate that between 5 and 6 inches of rain occurred over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported flooding near the intersection of Nolan Store Road and Beaverdam road, due to highwater from Beaverdam Creek. Radar estimates indicate that between 6 and 7 inches of rain occurred over the area, resulting in the flash flooding.

The Emergency Manager reported flooding of Riden Road from Big Sandy Creek. Radar estimates indicate that between 6 and 7 inches of rain occurred over the area, resulting in the quick rise of Big Sandy Creek and its tributaries, and the inundation of the roadway.
